findings.element: .b-item .b-grab rows, header buttons, .b-act Done / Take it off the plan, .b-undo
findings.problem: Driven at 1440, every control on the owner surface except the four date steppers is inert. I tabbed to each of the seven milestone rows and pressed Enter and Space, clicked each row, and dragged the row handle 120px up the measure: no editor opens, nothing moves, nothing changes. Change project, Add a moment, Preview, Publish, Send the link, Copy the link and Set the day all report NO CHANGE on click. Inside owner-editing, Done leaves the editor open (and jerks the page 0 to 16px), Take it off the plan leaves all seven items in place, Escape does not close, and the reversibility surface is a decoration: clicking its Undo button leaves the readout at 'in 16 days' and Ctrl+Z twice leaves it at 'in 9 days'. Worse, the visible affordance is the wrong object: the row is 520x79 with a 24px bold title, but the only button in it is the 54x28 'SHOWN' badge at the bottom left, and elementFromPoint over the title returns .b-title. So the owner can reach owner-editing only by editing the URL, and once there can only nudge a date. Fifteen named, focus-ringed, hover-styled controls promise verbs the direction does not have.
findings.fix: Make the whole row the control: move the button element to wrap the title, date and badge (a single .b-grab spanning the 520x79 row), and bind click, Enter and Space to open the inline editor for that item, so owner-flight reaches owner-editing without a URL. Bind Escape and the Done button to close the editor and return focus to the row's grab that opened it. Make Take it off the plan remove the item from the measure, reflow the remaining items, and push a real entry onto an undo stack. Make .b-undo's button and the Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z handler pop that stack and restore the prior date or the removed item, and update .b-undo's sentence to describe the change that is actually on top of the stack. Wire Add a moment to append a new undated item in the editor, Preview to swap the deck to state=desk, Publish to state=publish, Copy the link to navigator.clipboard.writeText of the share URL with the button label swapping to 'Copied' for 2s. Any control that will not be built this round must lose its button element and become inert text, not a focusable promise.

findings.element: state=day, and the absence of times and places everywhere
findings.problem: The whole body text of the wedding-morning screen is: 'TODAY / Mara & Finn / Saturday 3 October 2026 / Everything on the plan has happened. Nothing is left to count.' On the one morning the audience actually opens this, the product has nothing to say. There is no ceremony time, no arrival time, no address, no running order, no name of anyone to ring. This is structural, not a missing state: the data model on show is date-only. Not one surface in the whole set carries a clock time or a street, and the largest string a guest ever gets about place is the subtitle 'Wedding day at The Orchard'. The print keepsake has the same hole; the A4 that gets carried around on the morning prints a 79-day countdown, 'TODAY IS 16 JULY' and 'Nothing is planned for the next 16 days' instead of a running order. The brief puts 'the printed keepsake on the morning itself' in scope and the countdown vacates exactly there.
findings.fix: Give each item an optional time and place alongside its date, rendered as a second mono line under the title ('2.00pm · The Orchard, Adare') and included in the row's aria-label. Add a day plan to the fixture: the items that fall on the wedding date itself, ordered by clock time. Rebuild state=day so that when daysTo(theDay) === 0 the surface becomes that running order, hour by hour, with the venue address and one named contact under it, and the countdown collapses to the single word 'Today'. Rebuild state=print to render the same running order on page two of the A4 under the measure, so the printed sheet is usable on the morning rather than on the day it was printed.

findings.element: state=owner-empty, the day input and Set the day
findings.problem: The empty project asks one clean question and then refuses to answer it. The input's value is empty; '3 October 2026' is a placeholder, but it is set in the same grey mono the rest of the surface uses for real values, so it reads as a date already entered. Clicking Set the day with the field empty does nothing at all: no error, no hint, no focus move, no change of any kind on the page. A first-time owner cannot tell whether they have already set the day, whether they typed it wrong, or whether the product is broken, and there is nothing else on the screen to try. Under it, the header still offers Preview on a project with nothing to preview.
findings.fix: Replace the free-text field with input[type=date] plus a visible hint line 'For example 3 October 2026' below it, and drop the date-shaped placeholder so an empty field looks empty. On Set the day with no value, do not submit: keep focus in the field, set aria-invalid, and render one sentence under it, 'Pick the date of the day first.' On a valid value, write it to the fixture and move the deck to state=owner-flight with the measure drawn and focus on Add a moment. Remove Preview from the header while the project has no day set, or disable it with aria-disabled and the title 'There is nothing to preview yet.'

findings.problem: .b-edit paints background rgba(255,255,255,0.06) at z-index 2 over a measure whose items are positioned by date, so it reserves no band and hides nothing. Measured at 1440 the panel is 520x337 at (734, 656) and three live rows run straight through it: elementFromPoint over 'Final dress fitting' returns the '-7' stepper, and over 'Choose the evening music' returns the 'What guests see' label. On screen the owner is reading two sentences stacked on the same pixels while making the most consequential change the product offers. This is the floating-object class from the defect library, inverted: the panel does not erase what is under it, it is erased by it.
findings.fix: Give .b-edit an opaque ground (the ink ground at full alpha, or the paper ground when data-ground=paper) plus the existing hairline, and reserve its band in real layout: when an item enters editing, add the panel's measured height to the offset of every item below it on the measure for as long as the editor is open, so the rows part around it instead of running through it. Keep the strict day-to-pixel scale for the items themselves by applying the shift as a single translate on the group below the edited item, and restore it on close.

findings.element: state=phone, state=desk, state=print, the 'Nothing is planned' and 'Behind you' blocks
findings.problem: The guest surfaces are the owner's page with the chrome removed. The couple's family reads 'TODAY IS 16 JULY / Nothing is planned for the next 16 days.' as the loudest sentence on the screen, sitting directly under the one indigo rule, which spends the most prominent position on the page telling them nothing is happening. Below it they get 'BEHIND YOU / 2 done, the last of them 18 April. One thing is not going ahead.' -- second-person owner language addressed to someone who is not the owner, reporting a cancellation that is named nowhere, dated nowhere and reachable nowhere: neither the two completed items nor the cancelled one appears on the measure or in the tab order, so the only trace of three real events is an unnamed sentence. The blocks also swap order between widths (phone puts 'Behind you' after the measure, desk before it), so the same page tells its story in two different sequences. And the accessibility tree has exactly one heading on the whole surface, h2 'Behind you' -- the least important region on the page is the only landmark a screen reader user can jump to.
findings.fix: Split the copy by audience rather than by chrome. For phone, desk and print, replace the 'Nothing is planned' line with the next thing stated positively -- 'Next: menu tasting at The Orchard, Saturday 1 August, in 16 days' -- and cut the 'Behind you' block entirely from the guest surfaces. Keep it on the owner surfaces only, and make it real there: render the completed and cancelled items as a collapsed 'Behind you' list under the measure, each naming its title and date, with the cancelled one struck and labelled 'Not going ahead', so the sentence is a summary of things a person can actually see. Fix the reading order so 'Behind you' follows the measure at every width. Add an h1 carrying the couple's name and the day ('Mara & Finn, Saturday 3 October 2026'), demote 'Days away' to an h2 on the measure, and keep 'Behind you' as an h2 after it.

biggestWin: The thesis holds and it is worth keeping: a pixel is a real unit of time. The measure places every item strictly proportionally to how far away it is, so the fourteen-day gap between the fitting and the music is visibly twice the seven-day gap before it, and the emptiness of the next sixteen days is a shape you feel rather than a sentence you parse. It is paid for properly -- every count is derived from its own date through one accessor, the horizon number is the same number as the last item on the measure, and every surface that shows a date states today -- so the picture and the words cannot drift apart. Around it the register is disciplined and adult: one indigo rule and one indigo tick doing all the emphasis work, the 79 carried at a size no competitor would dare, print forced to paper, the ended link honest about what did and did not happen, and a loading frame that refuses to draw a measure it cannot yet place. That is a real idea with real craft under it. What is missing is the other half of the job -- the owner's verbs and the day itself.
